title: The proof decides
topic: A Rice University project puts a formal proof gate behind AI-proposed numerical algorithms
divergence_note: The camera lives inside one expanding mathematical derivation: candidate branches radiate from a Houston lab, contradictions shear away, and a white proof pulse travels through a machine-checkable gate. This is neither yesterday's rising field node nor the prior empty-seat void; its hero is a living proof tree in an instrument frame.

fingerprint.palette: Rice blue, proof white, Houston bayou green, graphite and contradiction magenta
fingerprint.metaphor: an AI-grown equation tree enters a formal proof press and only the certified branch leaves

fauna_scope.reason: No animal illustrates a formal proof, structured derivation, prompt variance, numerical algorithm or research-award start more precisely than the proof machine itself.

throughline.subject: one bright AI-proposed algorithm branch
throughline.opening_state: growing fast but carrying no guarantee
throughline.closing_state: waiting inside a prospective workflow with the proof seal still incomplete

scenes.what_moves: Candidate equations grow radially, one branch outruns the rest, and the proof gate closes across it by 1.1 seconds.

captions.text: At Rice University, the plan is for AI to propose numerical algorithms.
Lean will check their mathematical correctness and cost claims.
The National Science Foundation award starts on the fifteenth.
The project targets numerical linear algebra,
machinery beneath simulation, data analysis, and artificial intelligence.
Large language models and reinforcement learning will explore candidate designs efficiently.
But the award says those candidates can be opaque, inconsistent, and different across prompts.
LAAM is planned to represent each candidate as a structured mathematical derivation,
not a loose block of code.
The planned gate is Lean, certifying deterministic correctness and computational cost.
If that check succeeds, a machine proposal can become a reusable mathematical object with certificate-backed provenance.
The team plans applications from least squares to matrix completion.
This is a funded plan, not a published result.
Open software and public workshops are promised.
At Rice, the model gets a pencil.
In the plan, proof decides what becomes reusable.
